fields.body_md:
## About this programme

Looking at a computer science master's at Manchester? Here is what it costs, who can get in and the 2027 deadlines.

Manchester's closest course to an MSc Computer Science is the **MSc Advanced Computer Science**. It is a **12-month**, full-time course taught in person in Manchester, for 2027 entry.

**The most important fact for you:** this course is for computer science graduates with very high marks. It is not a conversion course.

The course has no compulsory units except your **60-credit** Masters Project. You choose four of ten themes. Each theme joins two related course units of 15 credits each, in areas such as cryptography, network security and computer architecture.

For the wider university, see our [University of Manchester page](/study-abroad/universities/university-of-manchester).

## Can you get in?

**Degree.** Successful applicants typically hold a First-class honours degree (**70%** average) in Computer Science, with at least **50%** Computer Science content. Manchester prefers students with the strongest grades from high-ranking institutions.

**Indian marks.** The course page says a typical Indian offer-holder has at least **65%**, or a First Class with Distinction depending on the institution, in a BSc Eng, BEng or BTech degree.

**GRE.** The course page does not mention GRE. GRE is a US-style graduate admissions test.

**English.** IELTS is an English language test. This course asks for **IELTS 7.0** overall with no subskill below **6.5**. Other accepted results include:

- TOEFL iBT: **100** overall, with no subskill under 22, or **5** overall on the new scale, with no subskill under **4.5**. Home Edition is not accepted.
- PTE Academic: **76** overall, with no subskill under 70

**ATAS.** ATAS (Academic Technology Approval Scheme) is a UK security clearance that some science and technology courses need before you get a visa. Manchester's course page does not say whether this course needs it. Ask the admissions team when you get your offer. If it is needed, an ATAS application takes at least **30 working days**.

## What it costs

Tuition for international students is **£41,400** per year, for entry in September 2027.

Manchester is outside London, so the outside-London visa rule applies. This is the worked first-year total.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Tuition for international students, September 2027 | £41,400 |
| Living money you must show for your visa: £1,171 × 9 months | £10,539 |
| Student visa application fee, from outside the UK | £558 |
| Immigration Health Surcharge for a visa of just over a year | £1,164 |
| **Total** | **£53,661** |

The sum is £41,400 + £10,539 + £558 + £1,164 = £53,661. Travel and housing are not included.

**Living money is money you show, not a fee.** The visa rule is **£1,171** for each month of your course outside London, up to **9 months**. You must hold this money for **28 days** in a row. The 28-day period must end within **31 days** of the date you apply. You do not pay it to the university.

**Health surcharge.** The Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) is a charge for using the NHS while you are in the UK. It is set by the length of your visa, not your course. For a course of 12 months or longer, the visa adds up to **1 month** before and **4 months** after the course. That makes a visa of more than a year but under 18 months. You then pay the yearly **£776** plus half of it, **£388**, so **£1,164**.

**Deposit.** Self-funded international applicants pay a deposit of **£2,500** before the university issues a CAS. Some applicants pay a higher deposit. A CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) is the electronic letter your visa application needs. The deposit is refunded only if your visa is refused.

**Application fee.** There is no application fee for this programme.

For the visa steps, read the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide). To plan the whole budget, use the [UK total cost breakdown](/study-abroad/study-in/uk/uk-total-cost-breakdown).

## Funding

- **Global Futures Scholarship for India:** **£12,000** off the published overseas tuition fee. It is for self-funded applicants domiciled in India with an offer for a full-time, on-campus master's starting September 2027. You must hold an offer and submit the online form by **25 April 2027**. Half the awards are made by **15 March 2027** and the rest by **1 June 2027**. Applicants whose bachelor's degree is from outside South Asia are not eligible. Read the [India scholarships page](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/country-specific-information/india/scholarships/).
- **Alumni discount:** Manchester and Manchester Metropolitan graduates get **10%** off master's tuition.

## Deadlines and intakes

Manchester uses staged admissions for September 2027 entry. You can apply at any stage, but earlier stages have more places.

| Stage | Application received by | Decision by |
|---|---|---|
| Stage 1 | 6 November 2026 | 8 January 2027 |
| Stage 2 | 1 January 2027 | 5 March 2027 |
| Stage 3 | 26 February 2027 | 30 April 2027 |
| Stage 4 | 21 May 2027 | 18 June 2027 |

Applications after 21 May 2027 are considered only if places remain. Deferred entry is not accepted: if you want the next year, you apply again.

## How to apply

1. **Check the entry rule.** You need a strong computer science degree with high marks.
2. **Take your English test.** Aim for IELTS 7 with no part below 6.5, or an accepted equivalent.
3. **Apply online** before your target stage date. Start from the [course page](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/courses/list/21573/msc-advanced-computer-science/).
4. **Apply for the Global Futures Scholarship.** The form is emailed after you get an offer. Submit it by 25 April 2027.
5. **Accept your offer and pay the deposit.** The university then issues your CAS.
6. **Check ATAS.** Ask the admissions team if the course needs an ATAS certificate.
7. **Apply for your visa.** You need your CAS, a current passport, proof of funds and your tuberculosis (TB) test result. India is on the UK's TB test list. The test must be at a clinic approved by the Home Office. Read the [TB test page](https://www.gov.uk/tb-test-visa/countries-where-you-need-a-tb-test-to-enter-the-uk) and the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide).

## After the programme

- **Work in the UK after your course.** The Graduate Route lets you stay and work in the UK after your studies. The visa lasts **2 years** if you apply on or before **31 December 2026**, and **18 months** if you apply on or after **1 January 2027**. A September 2027 student applies in 2028, so expect 18 months. The application fee is **£937**.

## Who it suits

**This programme is a strong choice if:**

- your BTech, BE or BSc is in computer science with at least 65% or First Class with Distinction
- you want to choose your own modules around a large project
- you can apply early in the staged cycle

**Think carefully if:**

- your degree is not in computer science, because the course is not a conversion course
- you need IELTS below 7, because the course asks for 7 with no part below 6.5

faq_json.q: Does Manchester offer a plain MSc Computer Science?
faq_json.a: Its closest course is the MSc Advanced Computer Science, a 12-month course for computer science graduates.

faq_json.q: How much does the Manchester MSc Advanced Computer Science cost for Indian students?
faq_json.a: Tuition is £41,400 per year for September 2027. Adding visa living money, the visa fee and the health surcharge gives £53,661 for the first year.

faq_json.q: What percentage do Indian students need?
faq_json.a: The course page says a typical Indian offer-holder has at least 65%, or First Class with Distinction, in a BSc Eng, BEng or BTech.

faq_json.q: Is there a scholarship for Indian students?
faq_json.a: Yes. The Global Futures Scholarship gives £12,000 off tuition to self-funded students domiciled in India. Submit the form by 25 April 2027.

faq_json.q: What IELTS score do I need?
faq_json.a: IELTS 7.0 overall with no subskill below 6.5. The course page does not mention GRE.
